clue.text: Collide with front of stationary three-wheeler

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, here taken from stationary

parts.note: a trike is a tricycle, a vehicle on three wheels

explanation.surface: A traffic accident: someone runs into a parked tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit or crash into something is a plain synonym for colliding with it.

clue.text: Support coercive measure

definitions.meaning: to give official approval or backing to something
a penalty imposed, for example on a state, to force compliance

explanation.surface: Backing a policy of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both official approval and a penalty, a famous pair of opposite senses.

clue.text: Field Spanish football team (first half only)

indicators.note: only the opening half of the team's name is kept, the first five of its ten letters

parts.note: Real Madrid is the famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Spain's top club fields its side for the first half of a match only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a verb for putting out a team; it is a noun, an area of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is a domain, sphere or province.

clue.text: Lively party in joint associated with drink

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
to sup is to drink, or a sup is a mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A rowdy party held in a pub that serves drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' hints at a bar or club; it is a body joint. A KNEES-UP is British slang for a boisterous party.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous celebration with dancing is a British colloquial name for a lively bash.

clue.text: Make possible arrest to intercept the Spanish Ecstasy

indicators.note: one piece intercepting another sits inside it, so the arrest word goes within the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
to nab someone is to arrest them
E is the usual short form for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drugs bust: police make possible an arrest by intercepting a Spanish shipment of ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow or make feasible is the standard dictionary sense of the verb.

clue.text: Gathers in information over savings

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so everything is read in reverse
in places the gathers word inside the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
to gather something is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone collects financial information about their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'over' do the work: in a down clue 'over' means read upwards, giving GGETSEN read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money put by for the future is a reserve fund, a nest egg.

clue.text: Pop devouring miserable specimen with sausage

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing up, so the pop word encloses the others

parts.note: to pop is to burst
a rat is a contemptible, wretched person

explanation.surface: Dad eats a sorry-looking sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like father but is the verb to burst.
explanation.definitionFit: This German fried sausage of pork or veal is one variety of banger.

clue.text: Large organisation in Ireland bringing in military police

indicators.note: bringing in means taking inside, so the Ireland word encloses the police abbreviation

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A big company in Ireland calls in the military police.
explanation.definitionFit: A large business group under one control is figuratively called a commercial domain or realm.

clue.text: American manoeuvres kept secret

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving things about, so the letters of American are rearranged

explanation.surface: American military manoeuvres were held in secrecy.
explanation.walkthrough: IN CAMERA is a legal term for proceedings held in private, out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearings held in private chambers, away from the public, are conducted confidentially.

clue.text: Versatile types, completely game

parts.note: all means wholly, completely
rounders is a British bat-and-ball game played in schools, similar to baseball

explanation.surface: People who can turn their hand to anything make for a complete game.
explanation.definitionFit: Players skilled at many things, such as cricketers who both bat and bowl, are adaptable people.

clue.text: Irritable agent ringing down

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the agent word goes round the down word

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
down, the soft fluffy surface, is nap, as on velvet

explanation.surface: A grumpy secret agent phones someone who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like an adjective for sad, but it is the soft pile on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappish, short-tempered person is quick to bite back, so testy or irritable.

clue.text: Thing I encountered upon retirement

indicators.note: retirement is drawing back, so the encountered word is read backwards

parts.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an object they came across once they had retired.
explanation.definitionFit: An article or object is a common synonym for a thing.

clue.text: Views rare broadcast about opener for Lancashire and what's in his trophy cabinet?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the initial
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of views rare are rearranged
the opener for a word is its first letter, here from Lancashire

explanation.surface: A cricket opener for Lancashire watches rare television footage of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a batsman, Lancashire being an English county cricket club, but it only supplies the first letter L. 'his' refers back to the Lancashire player.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophies such as cups and plates are prizes made of silver, the contents of a winner's cabinet.

clue.text: Good spoonerism made up about leader of group, a tattler

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the leading letter
made up means invented or put together, so the letters of spoonerism are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here from group

explanation.surface: A chatterbox invents a good spoonerism about the head of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: No sound swap here: 'spoonerism' is only anagram fodder. 'made up' turns it into OSSIPMONER, and 'about' wraps that round G from group's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler spreads rumour and tittle-tattle, someone who peddles idle talk.

clue.text: Son, little devil, revealed as dunce

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
to let on is to reveal or disclose

explanation.surface: A boy, a little rascal, is exposed as a dimwit.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish, slow-witted person is a dunce or fool.

clue.text: Friend to arrive shortly with army chaplain

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the arrive word loses its final letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive
padre is the forces' name for a military chaplain

explanation.surface: A friend is about to turn up with a regimental chaplain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells you to clip COME to COM.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish word for a comrade or buddy is used in American English for a mate.

clue.text: Greedy lot from Maine, with breeding

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
generation is the act of producing offspring, so breeding

explanation.surface: A breeding programme from Maine produces a greedy bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The ME GENERATION is a label for the self-absorbed young people of the 1970s and 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was coined for a cohort seen as selfish and acquisitive, hence a grasping bunch.

clue.text: Voluptuous beauty of grand old actress

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for grand, a thousand
Dorothy Lamour was a Hollywood film star of the 1930s and 1940s

explanation.surface: A grand old film star was known for her curvaceous good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluring, sensual attractiveness, the sex appeal of pin-ups, is called allure or charm.

clue.text: Fierce competition — artist's impression

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a trace is a mark or impression left behind

explanation.surface: A painter's view of a cut-throat contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a frantic, competitive struggle for success at work.

clue.text: Fearless loved one, disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so the middle letter of the loved one word is removed

parts.note: a darling is someone dearly loved

explanation.surface: A beloved person who has lost heart and become dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' looks like sad, but removes L, the heart of DARLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and adventurous, ready to take risks, so brave or fearless.

clue.text: Father, for example, holding post back in assembly

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the father word goes round the post word

parts.note: a father is one example of a parent

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the post word is read in reverse

parts.note: post is mail delivered by the postal service

explanation.surface: A father carries letters back into a meeting hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father, for example' is a definition by example, pointing to the broader class; 'holding' and 'back' then give the container and the turnaround of the post word.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative body such as Westminster is a national assembly of elected representatives.

clue.text: Better English head

parts.note: to better something is to cap it, outdoing it

explanation.surface: An English headmaster is held up as superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a person but a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland projecting into the sea is a promontory, which geographers call a head.

clue.text: Manage to protect small thicket

indicators.note: protecting something means wrapping round it, so the manage word encloses the small abbreviation

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Efforts are made to preserve a little patch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of trees or bushes growing closely together is a thicket or spinney.

clue.text: Restaurant in street described by writer

indicators.note: described in its sense of drawn around, so the writer encloses the street

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something to write with

explanation.surface: A restaurant on a certain street is reviewed by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is not an author but a pen; BIRO is the British everyday name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal eating place serving simple meals is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Running out of stock quickly?

parts.note: stock here means livestock, and cattle running away in a panicking herd fits the description

explanation.surface: A shop sells out of its goods in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The retail reading of stock is the decoy; it is cattle, running in a mass rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd of cattle or horses is what the clue pictures.

clue.text: Go after information exposing smart set

indicators.note: after places the go word behind the information word in the answer

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A journalist chases information that will expose high society.
explanation.definitionFit: People of good social position, the well-born class, form a fashionable elite.

clue.text: Night flight providing poor-quality whisky

definitions.meaning: an overnight passenger flight that leaves travellers bleary and bloodshot
an old American slang term for cheap, rough liquor

explanation.surface: Cheap whisky is served on an overnight plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are established: an overnight flight and slang for rotgut spirits.
